sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Om Prakash Rai,Ashish Rai
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri J.P.S. Chauhan, learned Aga and perused the
record.

2.  The present petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking quashing of charge sheet dated 2.7.2019 and the entire proceedings of Special trial No.654 of 2019, arising out of Case Crime No.2084 of 2007, under Sections 409, 419, 420, 467, 468, 171, 120-B IPC and Section 13(1)C(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station Kotwali, District Deoria.

entities.text: Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station Kotwali, District Deoria
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The petitioner was employed in the account section of the office of the Superintendent of Police.
In respect of gross irregularities and financial bungling, a departmental enquiry was conducted.

In the departmental enquiry, it was found that the petitioner was involved in financial bungling of Rs.13,48,490.30/- in one section and Rs.2,24,02,721.95 between his posting from 24.11.2000 to 28.9.2004.

On the basis of this finding, the FIR in question came to be registered and the police Ganga Sagar Giri vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23172414/
1 after investigating the offence, has filed the charge sheet.

entities.text: police Ganga Sagar Giri vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The charge sheet would disclose that there is more than prima facie case available against the petitioner for commission of the offence.
The power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has to be exercised sparingly in cases where no offence is made out even on the basis of allegations in the complaint/FIR/charge sheet.
In the present case, in the departmental inquiry as well as during course of investigation, involvement of the petitioner in financial bungling and embezzlement of huge amount has been found out.
5. In view thereof, this Court does not find it a fit case where this Court should exercise its inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the ongoing proceedings.
6. Thus, the present petition being devoid of merit and substance, is hereby dismissed.

7. However, it is provided that in case the petitioner surrenders before the concerned trial court within ten days from today and apply for bail, his bail application shall be considered and decided by the trial court expeditiously in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 21.2.2023 Rao/-
